feed.subtitle: Eunji Oh — PhD student in Music Technology at the Computational and Cognitive Musicology Lab (CCML), Georgia Tech.

entry.title: ISMIR 2024
entry.content:
The 25th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR) was held in San Francisco, CA.

I presented our paper: “Which audio features can predict the dynamic musical emotions of both composers and listeners?” with Hannah Kim and Kyung Myun Lee.
entry.summary: 25th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference

entry.title: SMPC 2024
entry.content:
The Society for Music Perception and Cognition (SMPC) conference was held in Banff, AB, Canada.

I presented: “Intermodal Analysis of Emotion Inference: Examining Shared Processes in Music and Social Contexts.”
entry.summary: Society for Music Perception and Cognition Conference

entry.title: KSMPC 2024
entry.content:
The 67th Conference of the Korean Society for Music Perception and Cognition (KSMPC) was held in Seoul.

I presented: “Emotion inference during music and social situations through empathic accuracy.”

Our lab also presented several other works:

  • Correlations between music experience and EEG responses (Park et al.)
  • Evaluation of AI-generated Music through Online Surveys (Kim et al.)
entry.summary: 67th Conference of the Korean Society for Music Perception and Cognition

entry.title: ICMPC 2023 (1)
entry.content:
The 17th International Conference on Music Perception and Cognition (ICMPC) was held in Tokyo, Japan.

I presented:

  • Musical pleasure revealed by electroencephalography theta oscillations: A systematic review
  • Effect of online music class on linguistic, cognitive, and musical abilities in Korean preschool children: A pilot study

Our lab also presented a comparison of melody interpolation by human and AI (Kim et al.).
entry.summary: 17th International Conference on Music Perception and Cognition (part 1)
